profile.short_bio:
About Me

Hi, I'm Haidong 👋! You can call me Andrew. I love robots and am dedicated to integrating them safely and reliably into our lives.

I am a second-year undergraduate at the University of Nottingham, pursuing a Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) degree. I am currently a visiting student in the Faculty of Computer and Mathematical Sciences at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, advised by Prof. Chenguang (Charlie) Yang (Fellow of IEEE/IET; Member of EASA and NAAI).

I also spent a wonderful summer at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology's Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute, under the supervision of Prof. Jun Ma. I am also an Undergraduate Researcher in the Robot Learning and Control Lab at Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo, advised by Prof. Xiaocong Li, and work closely with Dr. Haiyue Zhu from A*STAR.

Research Interests

My research interests lie at the intersection of robotic manipulation, generative models, and control theory, with a primary focus on dexterous manipulation and generative control policies. I am interested in how an understanding of geometric structure, contact interactions, and action consequences can inform policy learning and closed-loop control, enabling robots to adapt to changing environments, flexibly compose manipulation skills, and reliably accomplish long-horizon tasks. My long-term goal is to enable robust, safe, and sustained robot deployment at scale in real-world environments and to build intelligent systems that perceive, reason about, and interact with the physical world. More broadly, I am drawn to research that combines scientific impact with the potential to inspire new ideas.

publications.title: Opinion: Towards Unified Expressive Policy Optimization for Robust Robot Learning
publications.pub: EWM Workshop @ Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
publications.abstract: We propose UEPO to address limited behavioral coverage and distribution shift in offline-to-online reinforcement learning. It combines multi-seed diffusion sampling, dynamic divergence regularization, and trajectory augmentation to improve policy diversity and dynamics-model learning without training multiple policy models. D4RL evaluations report higher aggregate scores than Uni-O4 across locomotion, dexterous manipulation, and kitchen tasks.

publications.title: ALAS: Adaptive Long-Horizon Action Synthesis via Disentangled Environment and Self-State Representations
publications.abstract: ALAS addresses limited environmental transfer and skill reuse in long-horizon human–scene interaction. It disentangles environmental context from self-state dynamics and progressively integrates them through cross-attention, gated fusion, and mixture-of-experts fusion. Evaluations show improved cross-scene transfer and skill composition, faster long-horizon execution, and gains in learning efficiency on HumanoidBench.

publications.title: CoRDE: Concept-Prior Routed Diffusion Experts for Structural Generalization in Robot Manipulation
publications.highlight: Received a $1,500 travel grant from IEEE RAS.
publications.pub: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
publications.abstract: CoRDE addresses cross-task interference and unstable expert routing in multi-task manipulation. It combines concept priors with behavioral evidence through confidence-adaptive responsibility inference, while LoRA experts share a frozen diffusion backbone for parameter-efficient specialization. LIBERO and D3IL evaluations show improved task success, more stable expert allocation, and stronger behavioral diversity.

publications.title: Joint-Angle Invariance of Jacobian-Based Performance Indices for Serial Robotic Manipulators
publications.pub: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
publications.abstract: Joint-angle invariance (JAI) reduces the cost of Jacobian-based robot performance evaluation. We identify conditions under which selected manipulability and stiffness indices are independent of the first and last joint angles, enabling reduced-dimensional performance mapping and task-layout optimization. The demonstrated case reduces map-construction time from 163.887 to 1.723 seconds while preserving numerical accuracy.

publications.title: Preserving Operator Intent Under Actuation Constraints: Teleoperation of Manipulators with Coupled Transmissions
publications.pub: 5th Sensorimotor-Augmented Teleoperation Workshop @ IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
publications.abstract: Our actuator-constraint-aware teleoperation framework addresses motion distortion under coupled transmissions, gravity, and motor saturation. It combines coordinated actuator-space projection, gravity compensation, and continuous feasible-reference updates to preserve operator intent and reduce recovery transients. Real-robot experiments show smoother wrist motion, with 73.6% lower average velocity standard deviation than the no-gravity-compensation baseline.

publications.title: Consequence-Quotient Flow Matching for Robot Manipulation
publications.pub: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
publications.abstract: CQ-FM addresses the mismatch between action-coordinate errors and their task consequences. A learned consequence geometry guides both flow-matching training and safeguarded Gauss–Newton corrections with receding-horizon replanning, without enlarging the VLA backbone. Experiments show higher measured success in simulation and on hardware, including an increase from 69% to 78% across four real-robot tasks.

publications.title: Identifiability and Active Confirmation of Contact Mobility Transitions
publications.pub: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
publications.pub_note: RSS 2026 Workshop on Geometry of Motion (Oral Presentation).
publications.abstract: We characterize why passive contact observations can leave post-transition mobility ambiguous and derive identification-query requirements under an ideal projector model. Our active-confirmation pipeline combines transition detection, contact-state canonicalization, and targeted motion probes. Controlled MuJoCo noise audits using simulator-ground-truth eligibility report no incorrect geometry decisions, with safe aborts for ineligible cases.

publications.title: GeoPreserve: Preserving Action-Relevant Geometry in 3D Diffusion Policies for Long-Horizon Manipulation
publications.abstract: GeoPreserve addresses the loss of action-relevant geometry in compact 3D diffusion policies. Its Rewriting–Routing–Recovery design combines same-source density–depth views, relation-aware conditioning, and multi-scale denoising to preserve geometric distinctions throughout action generation. LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and D3IL evaluations show improved success and behavioral-mode coverage, with only 4.69% more parameters than the Mamba Policy backbone.

publications.title: MetaWorld-X: Semantic-Prior Expert Orchestration with Training-Time Latent Model-Based Improvement
publications.abstract: MetaWorld-X separates humanoid skill acquisition from semantic expert orchestration to reduce cross-skill interference. Human-motion-informed experts use imitation-constrained reinforcement learning and training-time latent-model improvement, while a VLM-supervised router refines semantic guidance through action compatibility and task returns. HumanoidBench evaluations show improved task returns and up to 3.8× faster foundational-skill convergence, without online planning at deployment.

publications.title: TA-SmolVLA: Tactile Tokens from Dense Force Fields for Contact-Rich Insertion
publications.pub: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
publications.abstract: TA-SmolVLA addresses visually occluded, contact-rich plug insertion by combining bilateral dense force-field tactile tokens with vision, language, and robot state. Its policy-to-control interface converts generated action chunks into filtered, error-limited equilibrium poses for Cartesian impedance control. Real-robot evaluation achieves 80% insertion success (16/20 trials), with dense tactile fields outperforming resultant-wrench inputs in stage-weighted performance across three policy backbones.

publications.title: A Ranking-Based Performance Normalization Method for Multi-Objective Robot Trajectory Optimization
publications.pub: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
publications.abstract: NRBPEM addresses scale imbalance and sensitivity to extreme values in multi-objective robot trajectory optimization. It combines rank-based normalization from sampled performance distributions with sequential weighted-sum optimization and simplified motion constraints. Simulated polishing and plotting studies show more robust normalization, reduced objective dominance, and faster convergence than min–max normalization while maintaining comparable trajectory performance.
